newsitem.title: CANADA: Quebec says 30,000 employees retiring early.
newsitem.headline: Quebec says 30,000 employees retiring early.

text.p: Almost 30,000 Quebec government employees are quitting the public service under the province's voluntary early retirement plan, a government official said on Wednesday.

"There were 28,982 departure requests and we will meet our deficit target," Louis Bourcier, political attache to the Quebec Treasury Board, told Reuters. "It will have an impact on the deficit, but we cannot measure it."
Quebec's Commission administrative des regimes de retraite et d'assurance (CARRA) said it expects another 1,000 employees to opt for early retirement in coming weeks.
The government had expected 15,000 employees to take advantage of the generous retirement plan by July 1.
The job cuts are part of austerity measures being implemented under the government's plan to cut its C$3.25 billion deficit to C$2.2 billion for fiscal 1997/98, which ends March 31.
To date, the departures include 10,600 employees from Quebec's health services sector, 10,300 from education and 3,000 from the civil service.

Quebec plans to hire 5,000 new teachers and 4,500 nurses over the coming weeks to replace some of those leaving. At March 31, the Quebec government had about 440,000 employees. ((Reuters Quebec City bureau 418-648-6442))
